Definition 2.2 (Zero-respecting first-order algorithm) . Let $(\boldsymbol{x}^{0},\boldsymbol{y}^{0})=(0,0)$ . For every $t\geq 0$ , let $\mathcal{S}_{x}^{t}:=\bigcup_{i=0}^{t}\left(\operatorname{supp}(\boldsymbol{x}^{i})\cup\operatorname{supp}(\boldsymbol{g}_{x}^{i})\right),\qquad\mathcal{S}_{y}^{t}:=\bigcup_{i=0}^{t}\left(\operatorname{supp}(\boldsymbol{y}^{i})\cup\operatorname{supp}(\boldsymbol{g}_{y}^{i})\right),$ where $(\boldsymbol{g}_{x}^{i},\boldsymbol{g}_{y}^{i})$ is the gradient response returned by the oracle at the $i$ -th query. A first-order algorithm is called zero-respecting if every feasible iterate $(\boldsymbol{x}^{t+1},\boldsymbol{y}^{t+1})\in X\times Y$ satisfies $\operatorname{supp}(\boldsymbol{x}^{t+1})\subseteq\mathcal{S}_{x}^{t},\qquad\operatorname{supp}(\boldsymbol{y}^{t+1})\subseteq\mathcal{S}_{y}^{t}.$

Definition 2.4 (Zero-respecting first-order algorithm) . Let $(\boldsymbol{x}^{0},\boldsymbol{y}^{0})=(0,0)$ . For every $t\geq 0$ , let $\mathcal{S}_{x}^{t}:=\bigcup_{i=0}^{t}\left(\operatorname{supp}(\boldsymbol{x}^{i})\cup\operatorname{supp}(\boldsymbol{g}_{x}^{i})\right),\qquad\mathcal{S}_{y}^{t}:=\bigcup_{i=0}^{t}\left(\operatorname{supp}(\boldsymbol{y}^{i})\cup\operatorname{supp}(\boldsymbol{g}_{y}^{i})\right),$ where $(\boldsymbol{g}_{x}^{i},\boldsymbol{g}_{y}^{i})$ is the gradient response returned by the oracle at the $i$ -th query. A first-order algorithm is called zero-respecting if every feasible iterate $(\boldsymbol{x}^{t+1},\boldsymbol{y}^{t+1})\in X\times Y$ satisfies $\operatorname{supp}(\boldsymbol{x}^{t+1})\subseteq\mathcal{S}_{x}^{t},\qquad\operatorname{supp}(\boldsymbol{y}^{t+1})\subseteq\mathcal{S}_{y}^{t}.$

Definition 2.5 (First-order zero-chain) . For $z\in\mathbb{R}^{d}$ , define $\operatorname{prog}_{0}(z):=\max\bigl(\{j\in[d]:z_{j}\neq 0\}\cup\{0\}\bigr).$ A differentiable function $F:\mathbb{R}^{d}\to\mathbb{R}$ is a first-order zero-chain if, for every $z\in\mathbb{R}^{d}$ , $\operatorname{prog}_{0}(\nabla F(z))\leq\min\{\operatorname{prog}_{0}(z)+1,d\}.$

Proposition 4.4 (Deterministic zero-respecting lower bound) . There exist universal constants $c_{\mathrm{d}},c_{\mathrm{acc}}>0$ such that, for every $L,D,\Delta>0$ and every $0<\varepsilon\leq c_{\mathrm{acc}}\min\{\sqrt{L\Delta},LD\},$ there exist finite-dimensional closed convex sets $\mathcal{X}_{\mathrm{d}},\mathcal{Y}_{\mathrm{d}}$ and an instance $F_{\mathrm{d}}:\mathcal{X}_{\mathrm{d}}\times\mathcal{Y}_{\mathrm{d}}\to\mathbb{R}$ defined in ( 4.11 ), which is jointly $L$ -smooth and concave in $y$ , satisfies $\operatorname{diam}(\mathcal{Y}_{\mathrm{d}})\leq D$ and $\Phi_{\mathrm{d}}(0)-\inf_{x\in\mathcal{X}_{\mathrm{d}}}\Phi_{\mathrm{d}}(x)\leq\Delta$ , where $\Phi_{\mathrm{d}}(x):=\max_{y\in\mathcal{Y}_{\mathrm{d}}}F_{\mathrm{d}}(x,y)$ . For every deterministic zero-respecting first-order algorithm, if its primal output $\widehat{x}\in\mathcal{X}_{\mathrm{d}}$ is obtained after $q<c_{\mathrm{d}}L^{2}D\Delta\varepsilon^{-3}$ calls to the exact-gradient oracle, then $S_{\mathrm{OS}}(\widehat{x})>\varepsilon,$ Consequently, the deterministic zero-respecting first-order oracle complexity of finding an $\varepsilon$ -stationary point is $\Omega\!\left(L^{2}D\Delta\varepsilon^{-3}\right).$

Proposition 4.7 . There are universal constants $c_{\rm s},c_{\rm acc}>0$ such that, under ( 4.19 ) and $0<\varepsilon\leq c_{\rm acc}\min\{\sqrt{L\Delta},LD\},$ the instance ( 4.14 ) belongs to $\mathcal{F}_{\rm NC\text{-}C}(L,\Delta,D)$ , and the sample function ( 4.17 ) defines an MSS oracle. Every zero-respecting algorithm using at most $c_{\rm s}\frac{L^{3}D^{2}\Delta\sigma^{2}}{\varepsilon^{6}}$ (4.21) shared-sample calls satisfies $\mathbb{E}S_{\rm OS}(\widehat{x})>\varepsilon$ .

Theorem 4.8 . There are constants $c,c_{0}>0$ such that the following holds. Let $L,\Delta,D>0$ , $\bar{L}\geq L$ , and $0\leq\sigma\leq D\bar{L}/4$ , and suppose that $0<\varepsilon\leq c_{0}\min\{\sqrt{L\Delta},LD\}.$ There is a hard instance in $\mathcal{F}_{\rm NC\text{-}C}(L,\Delta,D)$ , equipped with an unbiased stochastic gradient oracle of variance at most $\sigma^{2}$ and mean-square smoothness at most $\bar{L}$ , such that every zero-respecting randomized first-order algorithm using at most $c\left(\frac{L^{2}D\Delta}{\varepsilon^{3}}+\frac{L^{3}D^{2}\Delta\sigma^{2}}{\varepsilon^{6}}\right)$ (4.22) shared-sample oracle calls returns a primal output satisfying $\mathbb{E}S_{\rm OS}(\widehat{x})>\varepsilon$ . The expectation is over both oracle and algorithmic randomness.

Proposition 5.3 . Let $\kappa\geq 32L_{\rm d}$ and $0<\varepsilon\leq c_{\rm acc,d}\sqrt{L\Delta},\qquad c_{\rm acc,d}=\frac{c_{d}}{\sqrt{10240L_{\rm d}}}.$ There is a fixed deterministic instance in the NC–SC class of Definition such that every zero-respecting algorithm making at most $N\leq c_{\rm det}\frac{L\Delta\sqrt{\kappa}}{\varepsilon^{2}},\qquad c_{\rm det}=\frac{c_{d}^{2}}{10240L_{\rm d}\sqrt{8L_{\rm d}}},$ oracle calls satisfies $\|\nabla\Phi(\widehat{x})\|\geq 16\varepsilon$ .

Theorem 6.5 (Bounded-variance lower bound) . There are absolute constants $\kappa_{0},c_{\rm BV},c_{\rm acc}>0$ such that the following holds. Fix $L,\mu,\Delta>0$ and write $\kappa=L/\mu$ . For $\kappa\geq\kappa_{0}$ , $\sigma\geq 0$ , and $0<\varepsilon\leq c_{\rm acc}\sqrt{L\Delta}$ , there is one fixed instance and oracle in the NC–SC bounded-variance class for which every zero-respecting first-order algorithm using at most $N\leq c_{\rm BV}\left(\frac{L\Delta\sqrt{\kappa}}{\varepsilon^{2}}+\frac{L\Delta\kappa\sigma^{2}}{\varepsilon^{4}}\right)$ oracle calls satisfies $\mathbb{E}\|\nabla\Phi(\widehat{x})\|>\varepsilon$ .

Theorem 7.6 . There exist universal constants $\kappa_{0},c_{\rm MS}>0$ such that the following holds. Fix $L,\mu,\Delta>0$ , $\bar{L}\geq L$ , and $\sigma>0$ , and write $\kappa=L/\mu$ . Suppose that $\kappa\geq\kappa_{0}$ and that $0<\varepsilon\leq c_{\rm acc,d}\sqrt{L\Delta},$ where $c_{\rm acc,d}$ is defined in Proposition 5.3 . Assume also the stochastic accuracy range ( 7.3 ), with $a=\sqrt{\kappa/8}$ and the universal constants defined below. Then there is a fixed finite-dimensional instance and oracle in the NC–SC mean-square-smooth instance class of Definitions and 2.3 for which every zero-respecting randomized first-order algorithm using at most $N\leq c_{\rm MS}\left(\frac{L\Delta\sqrt{\kappa}}{\varepsilon^{2}}+\frac{\Delta\bar{L}\sigma\kappa^{3/2}}{\varepsilon^{3}}\right)$ shared-sample batch calls satisfies $\mathbb{E}\|\nabla\Phi(\widehat{x})\|>\varepsilon$ . The claim holds for every finite batch size and every primal output allowed by Definition 2.4 . The instance is chosen using only the problem parameters, independently of the algorithm and its randomness.

Remark 7.7 . When $\sigma=0$ , Proposition 5.3 and Lemma 7.5 give the deterministic $\Omega(L\Delta\sqrt{\kappa}/\varepsilon^{2})$ lower bound under the deterministic accuracy condition alone. The positive- $\sigma$ range ( 7.3 ) is used only for the Bernoulli-gated construction.
